test_title: PYST 22: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What defines land as “Culturable Wasteland” in land revenue records in India?

options.text: Land that is fallow for over five years

solution:
The correct answer is __**Land that is fallow for over five years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Culturable Wasteland:** In India, land recorded as "Culturable Wasteland" in revenue records refers to land that is **capable of cultivation** but has not been used for agricultural purposes for a prolonged period, specifically for **more than five years.**
 
• This category of land includes areas that have the potential for agricultural production but have been left uncultivated due to various reasons, such as **poor soil quality, lack of irrigation facilities, or socio-economic issues.**
 
• The classification of "Culturable Wasteland" ensures that such land is identified for possible reclamation and use in agricultural development programs.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is "Land that is fallow for over five years."*
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Urban infrastructure land:** This type of land is utilized for development purposes, such as construction of buildings, roads, and other urban facilities. It does not qualify as "Culturable Wasteland" because it is not suitable for agriculture.
 
• **Land under tree crops:** Land with tree crops is already in use for cultivation, particularly for horticulture or forestry. It cannot be categorized as wasteland.
 
• **Barren rocky land:** This type of land is unsuitable for cultivation due to its rocky terrain and poor soil quality. It is categorized separately and does not fall under "Culturable Wasteland."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Land Classification in India:** The land in India is categorized into various types based on its usage and productivity:

 
 
• **Cultivable Land:** Land that is actively used for agricultural purposes.
 
• **Culturable Wasteland:** Land that is arable but has been left uncultivated for a long time, typically for over five years.
 
• **Barren and Uncultivable Land:** Land that cannot be used for agriculture due to poor soil quality, rocky terrain, or other physical limitations.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Culturable Wasteland:**
 
 
• Such land can be reclaimed for agricultural production by improving soil fertility, providing irrigation, and addressing socio-economic challenges.
 
• It can also be used for plantation, forestry, or other sustainable practices to enhance its productivity.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has implemented various programs, such as the **Integrated Watershed Management Program (IWMP)**, to reclaim and improve wasteland for agricultural use.
 
• The **National Wasteland Development Board (NWDB)** was established in **1985** to identify and utilize wasteland effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Land Records:**

 
 
• Land revenue records play a crucial role in identifying the types of land and their utilization patterns.
 
• They help in planning land use, implementing agricultural policies, and managing resources effectively.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Culturable Wasteland in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Reclaiming such land can contribute significantly to increasing agricultural productivity in India.
 
• It is vital for achieving food security and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.
